name: Real analysis
description: Bounds, limits, continuity, integrals and convergence made exact, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Real analysis realm ("Real analysis"): bounds, sequences, series, continuity, derivatives, the Riemann integral and uniform convergence, for an
adult who has finished Foundations, Calculus 1, Calculus 2 and Logic and proof. Same Kepler outpost, now with a Standards Laboratory, where
Mira signs the certificates. The concept plan is docs/plans/REAL-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: The real line
chapters.blurb: Bounds, the least upper bound, distances, and how many numbers there are.

sector.name: Calibration Bench
sector.purpose: certify every reading the outpost relies on

chapters.name: Sequences
chapters.blurb: The exact meaning of a limit, with ε and N, and the sequences that must converge.

chapters.name: Cauchy sequences and series
chapters.blurb: Settling without knowing the limit, and exact promises about endless sums.

sector.name: Relay Station
sector.purpose: guarantee that long chains of corrections settle

chapters.name: Limits and continuity
chapters.blurb: ε–δ limits, continuity, its great theorems, and continuity that is uniform.

sector.name: Thermostat Hall
sector.purpose: promise that small input errors give small output errors

chapters.name: The derivative made precise
chapters.blurb: Differentiability, the mean value theorem, and guaranteed Taylor errors.

sector.name: Gauge Workshop
sector.purpose: bound how far every gauge can drift

chapters.name: The Riemann integral
chapters.blurb: Lower and upper sums, when they meet, and the integral's exact properties.

sector.name: Fuel Audit
sector.purpose: pin a total between two guaranteed bounds

chapters.name: Sequences of functions
chapters.blurb: Pointwise and uniform convergence, swapping limits, and distance in general.

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Every reading here is only as good as its certificate, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have what this needs from Foundations, the calculus courses and Logic and proof. I’ll work the first example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Close enough is not enough.
Learn to make every promise exact.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome to the Standards Laboratory. Calculus told us what limits are; here we prove that a reading really does settle, and we say exactly how close and from when. We start at the calibration bench with the smallest number above a whole set of readings.
copy.allDone: You did it. Every gauge, sum and simulation at the outpost carries a certificate you can defend line by line. Complex analysis comes next, where the same exact promises are made in the plane.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from bounds to uniform convergence. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the answer before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Make every promise exact.
help.intro: Real analysis starts where the calculus courses stop: limits were read from tables and intuition, and here every claim becomes precise. It asks for a bound, a supremum, an N or a δ that meets a stated ε, and it explains why such numbers exist. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Sets and proofs are never typed: a supremum, bound, N or δ, count or position is typed as a number, and a yes or no as 1 or 0.
